Let $m\ge0$ and $c>0$. Assume a temporal product chart with lapse-shift data $(N,\beta,h)$ as in [[def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data]], all four coordinates measured in metres. Write $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$ for $a,b\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ and let $g^{ab}$ denote the entries of the inverse matrix; then $p^\sharp:=\sum_{a,b=0}^3g^{ab}p_b\partial_a$ is the unique vector satisfying $g(p^\sharp,w)=p(w)$ for every tangent vector $w$. Put $T=\{t\in\mathbb R:ct\in I\}$. In every reduced expression below, $N$, $\beta^i$, $h_{ij}$ and $h^{ij}$ mean their pullbacks to $T\times\Omega$: $N(ct,q)$, $\beta^i(ct,q)$, $h_{ij}(ct,q)$ and $h^{ij}(ct,q)$, respectively. Thus $\kappa$, $p_0$ and $H$ are functions of $(t,q,p)$ on the massive reduced domain, or on its nonzero-spatial-momentum part when $m=0$; the spacetime metric and shell covector are evaluated at $(ct,q)$. On the future shell $C_m=\tfrac12(g^{ab}p_ap_b+m^2c^2)=0$, define

$$\kappa=\sqrt{m^2c^2+h^{ij}p_ip_j},\quad p_0=\beta^ip_i-N\kappa,\quad H(t,q,p)=-cp_0=c(N\kappa-\beta^ip_i).$$

For $m=0$, require $p_i\ne0$. Let $J=[t_1,t_2]$ satisfy $t_1<t_2$ and $[ct_1,ct_2]\subset I$, where $I$ is the first-coordinate interval of the temporal product chart; require the path $t\mapsto(ct,q(t))$ to stay in the chart. Take $q^i,p_i$ smooth on a neighborhood of $J$ and vary them by smooth one-parameter families that keep the paths in the chart, fix $q$ at both endpoints and vary $p$ freely; in the massless case the paths and sufficiently small variations stay in $p_i\ne0$. Then the gauge $x^0=ct$ reduces the first-order action to $\int_{t_1}^{t_2}(p_i\dot q^i-H)dt$, and its variational equations on the interior of $J$ are exactly $\dot q^i=H_{p_i}$, $\dot p_i=-H_{q^i}$. The construction is local to this chart and intervals transverse to its time slices; no global curved-space gauge or quotient is asserted.

countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Here $T$ denotes the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, called $N$ in that geometric definition. Use the distinction among a spacetime, a worldline, a pointwise observer, an observer congruence, a tetrad and a chart given in [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. This definition does not make $g$ dynamical.

At each $x\in M$, define $v^\flat:=g_x(v,\cdot)$ for $v\in T_xM$. Nondegeneracy of $g_x$ makes $\flat_x:T_xM\to T_x^*M$ an isomorphism; write $p^\sharp:=\flat_x^{-1}(p)$ for $p\in T_x^*M$, and define $g_x^{-1}(p,r):=g_x(p^\sharp,r^\sharp)$. In a chart, if $g_{ab}:=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$ and $(g^{ab})$ is its inverse matrix, then $p^\sharp=\sum_{a,b=0}^3g^{ab}p_b\partial_a$. A covector $p$ is **future causal** here exactly when $p^\sharp$ is a nonzero future-causal vector in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]].

In this relativistic-particle model, $m>0$ is a fixed **primitive mass parameter** measured in kilograms, and $c>0$ is a fixed **primitive conversion parameter** measured in metres per second. They are parameters of the adopted physical formulation, not quantities derived by this definition. Coordinates $x^a$ in an SI chart have length units; a cotangent vector $p=p_a\,dx^a$ has units of momentum, $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, when all four coordinates are in metres. The canonical one-form $p_a\,dx^a$ therefore has action units $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a $C^1$ curve; let $\lambda$ be its real parameter and write $V=d\gamma/d\lambda$. When $V$ is future timelike, set $s:=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$ and define the proper-time density by $d\tau=s\,d\lambda/c$. The tangent is then nonzero. If $\widetilde\lambda=f(\lambda)$ is an increasing $C^1$ reparametrization with $f'(\lambda)>0$, then $s_{\widetilde\lambda}=s_\lambda/f'(\lambda)$, so $s_{\widetilde\lambda}\,d\widetilde\lambda=s_\lambda\,d\lambda$. The length action $-mc\int s\,d\lambda$ has action units. For a future unit observer $n$ and future causal covector $p$, define the model normal-observer energy and spatial momentum covector by

$$E_n(p):=-c\,p(n),\qquad q_n(p):=p+p(n)n^\flat,$$

where $n^\flat=g(n,\cdot)$. We have $q_n(p)(n)=0$; write $n^\perp:=\{v\in T_xM:g_x(v,n)=0\}$. To verify the norm convention, choose a $g_x$-orthonormal basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $e_0$ future-directed (replace $e_0$ by $-e_0$ if necessary), and write $n=n^0e_0+\sum_{i=1}^3n^ie_i$ and $v=v^0e_0+\sum_{i=1}^3v^ie_i$. Use $n_s\cdot v_s:=\sum_{i=1}^3n^iv^i$, $|n_s|^2:=\sum_{i=1}^3(n^i)^2$, and $|v_s|^2:=\sum_{i=1}^3(v^i)^2$. The future-cone convention gives $n^0>|n_s|$, and $g_x(n,n)=-1$ gives $(n^0)^2=1+|n_s|^2$. If $g_x(v,n)=0$, then $v^0=(n_s\cdot v_s)/n^0$, so

$$g_x(v,v)=|v_s|^2-\frac{(n_s\cdot v_s)^2}{(n^0)^2}\ge\frac{|v_s|^2}{(n^0)^2}.$$

Here $|n_s|^2|v_s|^2-(n_s\cdot v_s)^2=\sum_{1\le i<j\le3}(n^iv^j-n^jv^i)^2\ge0$; if $v_s=0$, orthogonality also gives $v^0=0$. Thus $g_x$ is positive definite on $n^\perp$, and the isomorphism $\sharp_x$ carries covectors annihilating $n$ onto $n^\perp$, so $g_x^{-1}$ is positive definite on that covector subspace. Define $\|q_n(p)\|_n:=\sqrt{g_x^{-1}(q_n(p),q_n(p))}$. These are quantity definitions and unit conventions; they do not identify canonical momentum with mechanical momentum, assert that an apparatus measured these values, or establish a dynamical law.

A **temporal product chart** is a smooth diffeomorphism $\chi:U\to I\times\Omega$. Its coordinate functions $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$ are the four component functions of $\chi$. Spatial indices $i,j$ range over $1,2,3$, spacetime indices $a,b$ range over $0,1,2,3$, and repeated upper/lower indices are summed. We require $x^0$ and each $x^i$ to have length units in the physical interpretation.

The chart has **lapse-shift data** $(N,\beta,h)$ when $N:I\times\Omega\to(0,\infty)$, $\beta^i:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $h_{ij}:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ are smooth, $h_{ij}=h_{ji}$, and the matrix $(h_{ij})$ is positive definite at each point, with

$$g=-N^2(dx^0)^2+h_{ij}(dx^i+\beta^i dx^0)(dx^j+\beta^j dx^0).$$

Write $h^{ij}$ for the inverse matrix. The normal field is

$$n=N^{-1}(\partial_0-\beta^i\partial_i).$$

Direct contraction gives $g(n,n)=-1$; require that $n$ is future-directed in the supplied time orientation. This field of observers is distinct from the coordinate vector $\partial_0$, which may be spacelike. The coefficients $N,\beta^i,h_{ij}$ are dimensionless when all four coordinates are in metres. This definition is local to the specified product chart; it asserts no global temporal foliation.

Let $m\ge0$ and $c>0$. Assume a temporal product chart with lapse-shift data $(N,\beta,h)$ as in [[def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data]], all four coordinates measured in metres. $$\kappa=\sqrt{m^2c^2+h^{ij}p_ip_j},\quad p_0=\beta^ip_i-N\kappa,\quad H(t,q,p)=-cp_0=c(N\kappa-\beta^ip_i).$$

Then the gauge $x^0=ct$ reduces the first-order action to $\int_{t_1}^{t_2}(p_i\dot q^i-H)dt$, and its variational equations on the interior of $J$ are exactly $\dot q^i=H_{p_i}$, $\dot p_i=-H_{q^i}$. Adopt [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] and
[[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. Then the following conditional
physical claims hold in the flat classical model, with the units of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]].

**(a) Massive particle.** Let a massive particle have constant mass $m>0$,
four-momentum $P=mU$ and a future unit observer $n$. Its measured energy
$E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$, spatial momentum $q_n(P)=h(P)$ and kinetic energy
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ satisfy $E_n(P)>0$, $T_n(P)\ge0$ and the mass-shell
identity $E_n(P)^2=m^2c^4+c^2|q_n(P)|^2$; $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if the
particle is at rest in the observer's frame ($U=cn$). In an inertial frame
whose stationary observer is $n=e_0$, the components are $P=(E/c,\mathbf p)$
with $E=E_{e_0}(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $\mathbf p=m\gamma_w\mathbf w\in\mathbb R^3$
the coordinates of $q_{e_0}(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3p^ie_i$
for the coordinate velocity $\mathbf w$, and under a passive boost the
components transform as the components of the vector $P$; the combination
$E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m^2c^4$ is frame-independent.

**(b) Four-force.** Along a $C^2$ worldline with four-acceleration $A$, the
four-force $F=\dot P$ satisfies $\eta(P,F)=0$ and $F=mA$; in an inertial frame
$F=\gamma\,(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\ \mathbf f)$ and
$dE/dt=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$, where $\mathbf f=d\mathbf p/dt$ is the
coordinate three-force. The constancy of $m$ is used; if instead $m$ is a
$C^1$ function $m:I\to(0,\infty)$ along the same worldline, define $P:=mU$
and $F:=\dot P$ by the general derivative construction. As a mathematical identity, $\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,dm/d\tau$, and the
constant-mass identities are not transferred to variable-mass systems.

**(c) System mass.** For a finite nonempty system of particles all of whose
four-momenta are nonzero future causal, let $Q:=\sum_iP_i$. If $Q$ is
future timelike, its invariant mass $M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$ satisfies: in the
center-of-momentum frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ one has
$Mc^2=\sum_iE_{e_0}(P_i)$; every massive constituent has
$E_{e_0}(P_i)\ge m_ic^2$, with equality exactly when it is at rest in that
frame, and every massless constituent has $E_{e_0}(P_i)>0$. Hence
$M\ge\sum_im_i$ over the massive constituents, with equality if and only if
the system is massive-only and all its constituents are at rest in the
center-of-momentum frame. If $Q$ is future null, then $M=0$, all constituents
are massless with parallel momenta, and no center-of-momentum frame exists.

**(d) Massless particle.** An ideal massless particle has
$E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$, has no rest frame and is not $mU$ for any $m>0$; it is
not obtained from the massive formula by setting $m=0$.

**(e) Necessary collision thresholds.** Suppose that, under the adopted
isolated-collision balance, an isolated collision occurs whose incoming legs
are massive particles of constant masses $m_1,\dots,m_N$ and whose outgoing
legs are massive particles of masses $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_K$ and possibly ideal
massless particles. Let $M$ be the invariant mass of the common total
four-momentum $Q$. Then the necessary inequalities $M\ge\sum_im_i$ and
$M\ge\sum_j\mu_j$ hold; if the incoming side is a projectile of mass $m_1$
and a target of mass $m_2$ at rest in the observer frame of the target, with
projectile energy $E$ and kinetic energy $T=E-m_1c^2$ in that frame, then

$$E\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^K\mu_j\Bigr)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2\Bigr],\qquad T\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^K\mu_j\Bigr)^2-(m_1+m_2)^2\Bigr],$$

Separately, under the same adopted balance, a single incoming massless particle
cannot produce an outgoing state containing a massive particle. These are kinematic necessity statements under
the adopted conservation: they do not assert that any collision occurs, do
not fix probabilities, amplitudes or cross sections, and are not empirical
findings.

**(f) Scope.** All clauses are conditional on the two postulates and on the
stated idealisations; the conclusions carry the same idealisations. No
measurement, precision, statistical or empirical claim is made.

2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;

   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
